example.description:
Whether to generate simplified, example-style data rather than the full possible range of values.
For example this will produce a simple value like "17" for an `int` rather than a uniform random number in
[-2⁶³..2⁶³).

This is only relevant for untrained models, such as {@link DataGenObj} and {@link DataGenPrimitive}.

seed.description:
Initial seed value for randomization. Note that generators with same seed are required to produce exact same
sequence of values. This value is mutated as methods are called on it; see #next and #array.

values.description: Possible values to pick a candidate from.

params.description: The parameters with which the data generator was trained (if any).

precision.description:
For some scalar values, values are produced with the appropriate amount of precision.
Notably, this affects `decimal` and `datetime` values.

title:
Type for generating scalar (primitive) values uniformly distributed within a range. Note that not all primitives
are scalars, only numbers (`int`, `double`, etc) and `datetime` are supported.
name: DataGenUniform
